newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech govt approves Slovak Jewish gold payment.
newsitem.headline: Czech govt approves Slovak Jewish gold payment.

text.p: The Czech government has agreed to pay 20 million crowns ($580,000) to a Jewish foundation in settlement of claims on gold and jewels belonging to Slovak Jewish Holocaust victims held in the Czech National Bank.
Deputy Foreign Minister Karel Kovanda said on Thursday the government had approved the payment on Wednesday and that it would be made as soon as a bank account was set up.
"What I see in this is the importance of taking care of one of the residues of the Holocaust, a residue where the moral issue was never in doubt," Kovanda told a news conference.
The gold and jewels were among valuables confiscated from Slovak Jews during the war which were eventually transferred into the former Czechoslovak state bank's vaults.
Kovanda said the Czech Finance Ministry had valued the gold and jewels at 32 million crowns and that the Czechs would pay something in excess of 20 million.
Under the formula used for dividing the assets of the former Czechoslovakia, which split into the Czech Republic and Slovakia in 1993, the Czechs would pay two thirds of the total.

"We have not engaged the Slovak authorities directly. It is for the Slovak Jewish community to do so and we have precious little indication of how Slovak governmental and banking authorities will react," Kovanda said.
He said negotiations, over several months, had been undetraken with the cooperation of the Slovak Jewish community.
Jozef Weiss, a Holocaust survivor and director of the Slovak Union of Jewish Commnunities said he was satisfied.
"The entire sum will come to Slovakia and we will set up a foundation with the Czechs to distribute the money," he said.

The foundation, formed jointly by the Slovak and Czech Jewish communities, would focus on charitable projects such as a home for the chronically sick and the maintenance of Slovakia's approximately 630 Jewish cemeteries.
"If the dead could talk, we would want the foundation to focus on things with which the dead were bound to agree," Kovanda said.
Before World War Two, the Slovak part of Czechoslovakia had 70,000 Jews. It became nominally independent under Catholic priest Jozef Tiso, a puppet of Nazi Germany.
The Slovak state paid the Nazis 500 marks per head to cover the cost of "removing" Jews to extermination camps. The community today numbers only 3,000.

The valuables were stored in the then Slovak national bank. Records show there were 80,000 pieces. After the war, only 4,000 pieces were returned and the rest were transferred in 1953 to the Czechoslovak state bank.
Previously the volume of gold has been in dispute. Weiss said last year it was in the "hundreds of kilos" while the Czechs said last year it was around 50 kg.
"Whatever the volume, the translation into currencies was not really disputed," Kovanda said. ($=34.5 Czech crowns)
